newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Dollar higher against yen but gains capped.
newsitem.headline: Dollar higher against yen but gains capped.

text.p: The dollar remained on firm footing against the yen but gave up its early highs as buying interest in the mark/yen cross faded, dealers said on Monday.
They said trade was thin and directionless with Tokyo players out for a holiday and no fresh leads in the market.
"The markets are very thin. Tokyo's off so anyone who's got anything to do is just going to push the market around," a European bank dealer said.
He said the dollar was likely to remain confined to its recent ranges ahead of U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on Tuesday.
The dollar was expected to be well supported around 115.25 yen and 1.7850 marks but face resistance above 116.00 yen and 1.7920 marks during the Asian session, dealers said.
"There should be Japanese exporter (sell) orders from 115.80 to 116.00 yen," another European bank dealer said.
Dealers said the dollar could come under pressure against the mark after its repeated failure to make a renewed attempt on the 1.80 marks level.
"If the dollar breaks below 1.7850 marks, there's some leeway to 1.7740 but it should not fall below there. That would take out the technical bull run," a dealer said.
He said such a move could push the dollar out of its recent 1.75-1.80 marks range and would prompt players to reduce their long positions. -- Sonali Desai (65-8703090)
